findings.title: [P1] Revert to argv-based `execFile` to close shell injection via `branch`
findings.body: `execAsync` runs its argument through a shell, so any shell metacharacters in `branch` are executed rather than treated as a ref name: `showBranch("main; rm -rf /tmp/x")` runs `git show main` and then `rm -rf /tmp/x` under the process's identity; `$(...)`, backticks, and `&&` work the same way. Because `branch` is the parameter of an exported API with no validation (and no in-repo callers constraining it), any caller that passes user-influenced input — the normal case for branch names — gets arbitrary command execution. It also breaks the error contract: `showBranch("missing; true")` resolves successfully even though `git show` failed, because the trailing command's exit status wins. The removed `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])` was injection-safe and should be restored.

findings.title: [nit] Remove now-unused `execFile` import and `execFileAsync` binding
findings.body: After the switch, `const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)` (line 4) is never used, leaving the `execFile` import and the binding as dead code. If the P1 fix restores `execFileAsync`, this resolves itself; otherwise drop both.
